headline: US stocks trade mixed as chip sell-off deepens on AI and China concerns while investors rotate into cyclicals and defensives on solid earnings
raw_text:
- PHLX Semiconductor Index falls nearly 6% as a heavy chip sell-off extends on persistent AI spending doubts, fears of circular data-center financing, intensifying China competition and global memory-chip weakness after the Kospi decline
- Micron Technology (MU), SK Hynix (SKHY), Intel (INTC), Nvidia (NVDA), Sandisk (SNDK), Arm Holdings (ARM), Teradyne (TER) and Corning (GLW) down more than 14% premarket
- Coca-Cola (KO) jumps over 7% after reporting strong earnings and raising its full-year revenue and profit forecasts on robust soda demand
- Sherwin-Williams (SHW) rallies about 8% on strong earnings, supporting rotation into cyclicals
- Boeing (BA) climbs roughly 3% as investors look past a loss tied to a $280 million Air Force One charge and focus on upbeat revenue, backlog, positive free cash flow and an improving outlook
- Healthcare and financials push to record highs, while industrials, consumer defensives, staples and real estate outperform and technology and semiconductors lag sharply
- Centene (CNC) trades lower despite delivering a Q2 earnings beat and raising guidance
- June US goods trade deficit comes in slightly better than feared, with limited market reaction
- Apple (AAPL) briefly tops a $5 trillion market capitalization during the session
- S&P 500 (SPY) edges higher alongside a stronger Dow (DIA) as investors rotate out of chip names, while the Nasdaq (QQQ) and Russell 2000 (IWM) slip
